     6	The damped occupation kernel and its exact row maximum, from
     7	`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` (revision 3920258):
     8	the kernel `K_⋆` of `E:occupation-damped-kernel` (lines 282-289) and
     9	Lemma `L:occupation-kernel-row` (lines 291-309, display
    10	`E:occupation-kernel-row`, lines 295-298).
    11	
    12	Standing assumptions of the section (lines 4-10): a nonzero original
    13	covariance from `H:homog`, `a = α₀`, `q = 4 - α`, `D = q - 2a > 0`.
    14	
    15	Formalized here (all proved, no supplied input):
    16	* `Kstar a D u`: the manuscript's formula
    17	  `K_⋆(u) = Γ_E(a)⁻¹ ∫_0^∞ e^{-(λ + λ²/(2D))|u|} λ^{a-1} dλ` for `u ≠ 0`,
    18	  and `K_⋆(0) = 0` (line 289); `Γ_E` is Mathlib's `Real.Gamma`.
    19	  `Kstar_eq_Psi` identifies it, for `u ≠ 0`, with the averaged clock kernel
    20	  `TimeFractional.Psi a |u| (|u|/D)` of the main file, and
    21	  `kstarIntegrand_integrable` proves that the defining integral is a
    22	  convergent Lebesgue integral for `u ≠ 0`, `a > 0`, `D > 0` (so `Kstar` is
    23	  not a junk value of a non-integrable Bochner integral there).
    24	* `occupation_kernel_row`: the kernel is even, positive off zero, locally
    25	  integrable (`a < 1`), strictly decreasing on `(0,∞)`, `K_⋆(u) ≤ |u|^{-a}`
    26	  off zero; for every `s ∈ [0,1]` the row `t ↦ K_⋆(s-t)` is integrable on
    27	  `[0,1]`; and `R_⋆ = 2 ∫_0^{1/2} K_⋆` is the greatest element of the set of
    28	  row values `{∫_0^1 K_⋆(s-t) dt : s ∈ [0,1]}` (so the maximum exists and
    29	  equals `R_⋆`, attained at `s = 1/2`), with `K_⋆` integrable on `[0,1/2]`
    30	  and `0 < R_⋆` (a real number, hence finite).
    31	* `occupation_kernel_row_paper`: the same under the section's standing
    32	  hypotheses, `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d α a Γ μ`, `Γ ≠ 0` and
    33	  `D = (4 - α) - 2a`; `D > 0` is derived there from `H:homog`
    34	  (`a + α < 2`).  `Γ ≠ 0` is carried as stated by the TeX and is not used
    35	  by the proof.
    36	
    37	Also formalized (all proved, no supplied input), Lemma `L:spatial-physical-pair`
    38	(lines 12-33, display `E:spatial-physical-pair`, lines 15-17):
    39	* `pairMeasure Γ = volume.prod Γ` (`ν(dx,dy) = dx Γ(dy)`) and
    40	  `pairing Γ f h = ∫⁻ f(x) h(x-y) dν` for `[0,∞]`-valued `f, h` (the TeX's
    41	  "extended nonnegative integral"; arbitrary `[0,∞]`-valued functions are
    42	  allowed, which contains the TeX's finite Borel representatives);
    43	* `spatial_physical_pair` (for any locally finite `Γ` on `ℝ^d`): `ν` is
    44	  sigma-finite; `pairing` is unchanged when `f` and `h` are replaced by
    45	  Lebesgue-a.e. equal functions; for Lebesgue-a.e. measurable `f, h` the
    46	  integrand is `ν`-a.e. measurable; Lebesgue-a.e. convergence of a sequence of
    47	  real functions transfers to `ν`-a.e. convergence at `x` and at `x - y`.
    48	  `ae_pair_of_ae` is the null-set transfer of the TeX proof (lines 26-29);
    49	* `spatial_physical_pair_paper`: the same under `HomogCovariance d α a Γ μ`
    50	  and `Γ ≠ 0`; only local finiteness of `Γ` is used.
    51	
    52	The manuscript says "decreasing"; the Lean statement proves strict decrease
    53	(`StrictAntiOn`), which implies the weak form.  Interval integrals are
    54	Mathlib's `∫ t in (0:ℝ)..1`, and each comes with its integrability.
    55	
    56	Proof route.  The bound `K_⋆ ≤ |u|^{-a}` and positivity are reused from
    57	`TimeFractional.Psi_le_rpow` and `TimeFractional.Psi_pos`.  The row identity
    58	`∫_0^1 K_⋆(s-t) dt = Φ(s) + Φ(1-s)` with `Φ(t) = ∫_0^t K_⋆` is the TeX's.
    59	The TeX then invokes concavity of `Φ`; here the inequality
    60	`Φ(s) + Φ(1-s) ≤ 2Φ(1/2)` (for `s ≤ 1/2`, the other case by `s ↦ 1-s`) is
    61	proved directly by a shift comparison,
    62	`Φ(1-s) - Φ(1/2) = ∫_s^{1/2} K_⋆(x + (1/2 - s)) dx ≤ ∫_s^{1/2} K_⋆ =
    63	Φ(1/2) - Φ(s)`, using that `K_⋆` decreases on `(0,∞)` (the same fact that
    64	the TeX uses for concavity).  Lemmas marked "auxiliary to the Lean proof
    65	route" have no manuscript label.
    66	-/

    84	/-! ### The kernel `K_⋆` (`E:occupation-damped-kernel`, lines 282-289) -/
    85	
    86	/-- The integrand of `E:occupation-damped-kernel`:
    87	`e^{-(λ + λ²/(2D))|u|} λ^{a-1}` (lines 284-287). -/
    88	def kstarIntegrand (a D u l : ℝ) : ℝ :=
    89	  Real.exp (-(l + l ^ 2 / (2 * D)) * |u|) * l ^ (a - 1)
    90	
    91	/-- The kernel `K_⋆` of `E:occupation-damped-kernel` (lines 282-289):
    92	`Γ_E(a)⁻¹ ∫_0^∞ e^{-(λ + λ²/(2D))|u|} λ^{a-1} dλ` for `u ≠ 0`, and
    93	`K_⋆(0) = 0`. -/
    94	def Kstar (a D u : ℝ) : ℝ :=
    95	  if u = 0 then 0 else (Real.Gamma a)⁻¹ * ∫ l in Ioi (0 : ℝ), kstarIntegrand a D u l
    96	
    97	/-- The row integral `∫_0^1 K_⋆(s-t) dt` of `E:occupation-kernel-row`. -/
    98	def row (a D s : ℝ) : ℝ := ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, Kstar a D (s - t)
    99	
   100	/-- `R_⋆ = 2 ∫_0^{1/2} K_⋆(u) du` of `E:occupation-kernel-row`. -/
   101	def Rstar (a D : ℝ) : ℝ := 2 * ∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..(1 / 2), Kstar a D u
   102	
   103	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. The integrand equals the integrand of
   104	`TimeFractional.Psi a |u| (|u|/D)` (an identity of real numbers, valid for every `D`). -/
   105	theorem kstarIntegrand_eq_psiKernel (a D u l : ℝ) :
   106	    kstarIntegrand a D u l = psiKernel a |u| (|u| / D) l := by
   107	  unfold kstarIntegrand psiKernel
   108	  rw [mul_comm]
   109	  congr 2
   110	  ring
   111	
   112	/-- For `u ≠ 0`, `K_⋆(u) = Ψ_a(|u|, |u|/D)`, the averaged clock kernel
   113	`TimeFractional.Psi` of `E:averaged-clock-kernel` (main file, line 7503). -/
   114	theorem Kstar_eq_Psi (a D u : ℝ) (hu : u ≠ 0) : Kstar a D u = Psi a |u| (|u| / D) := by
   115	  simp only [Kstar, hu, ite_false, Psi, kstarIntegrand_eq_psiKernel]
   116	
   117	/-- For `a > 0`, `D > 0`, `u ≠ 0`, the integrand of `E:occupation-damped-kernel` is
   118	integrable on `(0,∞)`. -/
   119	theorem kstarIntegrand_integrable (a D u : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hD : 0 < D) (hu : u ≠ 0) :
   120	    Integrable (kstarIntegrand a D u) L0 := by
   121	  have h := psiKernel_integrable a |u| (|u| / D) ha (abs_pos.2 hu) (by positivity)
   122	  have he : kstarIntegrand a D u = psiKernel a |u| (|u| / D) :=
   123	    funext (kstarIntegrand_eq_psiKernel a D u)
   124	  rw [he]
   125	  exact h
   126	
   127	/-- `K_⋆` is even. -/
   128	theorem Kstar_neg (a D u : ℝ) : Kstar a D (-u) = Kstar a D u := by
   129	  simp only [Kstar, neg_eq_zero, kstarIntegrand, abs_neg]
   130	
   131	/-- `K_⋆(u) > 0` for `u ≠ 0` (`a > 0`, `D > 0`). -/
   132	theorem Kstar_pos (a D u : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hD : 0 < D) (hu : u ≠ 0) : 0 < Kstar a D u := by
   133	  rw [Kstar_eq_Psi a D u hu]
   134	  exact Psi_pos a |u| (|u| / D) ha (abs_pos.2 hu) (by positivity)
   135	
   136	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. `K_⋆(u) ≥ 0` for every `u` (`a > 0`, `D > 0`). -/
   137	theorem Kstar_nonneg (a D u : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hD : 0 < D) : 0 ≤ Kstar a D u := by
   138	  by_cases hu : u = 0
   139	  · simp [Kstar, hu]
   140	  · exact (Kstar_pos a D u ha hD hu).le
   141	
   142	/-- `K_⋆(u) ≤ |u|^{-a}` for `u ≠ 0` (`a > 0`, `D > 0`). -/
   143	theorem Kstar_le_rpow (a D u : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hD : 0 < D) (hu : u ≠ 0) :
   144	    Kstar a D u ≤ |u| ^ (-a) := by
   145	  rw [Kstar_eq_Psi a D u hu]
   146	  exact Psi_le_rpow a |u| (|u| / D) ha (abs_pos.2 hu) (by positivity)
   147	
   148	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. Strict decrease of `Ψ_a(r, r/D)` along the
   149	diagonal `r ↦ (r, r/D)`, for `0 < r < r'`. -/
   150	theorem Psi_diag_strictAnti (a D r r' : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hD : 0 < D) (hr : 0 < r)
   151	    (hrr : r < r') : Psi a r' (r' / D) < Psi a r (r / D) := by
   152	  have hr' : 0 < r' := hr.trans hrr
   153	  have hv : 0 ≤ r / D := by positivity
   154	  have hv' : 0 ≤ r' / D := by positivity
   155	  have hvv : r / D ≤ r' / D := div_le_div_of_nonneg_right hrr.le hD.le
   156	  have i1 := psiKernel_integrable a r (r / D) ha hr hv
   157	  have i2 := psiKernel_integrable a r' (r' / D) ha hr' hv'
   158	  have hpos : ∀ᵐ l ∂L0, 0 < psiKernel a r (r / D) l - psiKernel a r' (r' / D) l := by
   159	    refine (ae_restrict_iff' measurableSet_Ioi).2 (Eventually.of_forall fun l hl => ?_)
   160	    have hl : 0 < l := hl
   161	    rw [sub_pos]
   162	    unfold psiKernel
   163	    refine mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left (Real.exp_lt_exp.2 ?_) (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hl _)
   164	    have h1 : r * l < r' * l := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hrr hl
   165	    have h2 : r / D * l ^ 2 / 2 ≤ r' / D * l ^ 2 / 2 := by
   166	      have := sq_nonneg l
   167	      have : r / D * l ^ 2 ≤ r' / D * l ^ 2 := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hvv this
   168	      linarith
   169	    linarith
   170	  have h := integral_pos_of_ae_pos
   171	    (f := fun l => psiKernel a r (r / D) l - psiKernel a r' (r' / D) l) (i1.sub i2) (by simp) hpos
   172	  rw [integral_sub i1 i2, sub_pos] at h
   173	  unfold Psi

    39	* `pairMeasure Γ = volume.prod Γ` (`ν(dx,dy) = dx Γ(dy)`) and
    40	  `pairing Γ f h = ∫⁻ f(x) h(x-y) dν` for `[0,∞]`-valued `f, h` (the TeX's

    33	/-- A tempered measure: `∫ (1 + ‖x‖)^(-k) dν < ∞` for some natural `k`. -/
    34	def IsTempered {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    35	  ∃ k : ℕ, ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + ‖x‖) ^ (-(k : ℝ))) ∂ν < ⊤
    36	
    37	/-- An even measure: invariant under `x ↦ -x`. -/
    38	def IsEven {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    39	  ν.map (fun x => -x) = ν
    40	
    41	/-- Positive-definiteness of `Γ` as a tempered distribution:
    42	`⟨Γ, φ ⋆ φ̃⟩` is a nonnegative real for every Schwartz `φ`, where
    43	`(φ ⋆ φ̃)(x) = ∫ φ(x + y) conj(φ(y)) dy` and `φ̃(x) = conj(φ(-x))`. -/
    44	def IsPosDefDistr {d : ℕ} (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    45	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    46	    (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).im = 0 ∧
    47	      0 ≤ (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).re
    48	
    49	/-- `μ` is the spectral measure of `Γ` in the manuscript's convention
    50	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)` in the sense of tempered distributions:
    51	`∫ φ dΓ = ∫ (∫ φ(x) e^{i ξ·x} dx) μ(dξ)` for every Schwartz `φ`. -/
    52	def IsSpectralMeasure {d : ℕ} (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    53	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    54	    ∫ x, φ x ∂Γ =
    55	      ∫ ξ, (∫ x, φ x * Complex.exp (Complex.I * (inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ))) ∂μ
    56	
    57	/-- Hypothesis `H:homog`. Let `d ∈ {1,2,3}` and `0 < α₀ < 1`. The spatial
    58	covariance is a nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure
    59	`Γ` on `ℝ^d` with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure `μ`,
    60	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)`; for every Borel set `A` and `c > 0`,
    61	`Γ(cA) = c^{d-α} Γ(A)`; `α₀ + α < 2` (`E:threshold`), with `0 < α < d` or
    62	`α = d = 1`. A Lean measure is nonnegative, and on `ℝ^d` a locally finite
    63	Borel measure is a Radon measure. -/
    64	structure HomogCovariance (d : ℕ) (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) :
    65	    Prop where
    66	  dim : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3
    67	  alpha0_pos : 0 < alpha0
    68	  alpha0_lt_one : alpha0 < 1
    69	  Γ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ
    70	  Γ_even : IsEven Γ
    71	  Γ_tempered : IsTempered Γ
    72	  Γ_posdef : IsPosDefDistr Γ
    73	  μ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ
    74	  μ_even : IsEven μ
    75	  μ_tempered : IsTempered μ
    76	  spectral : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ
    77	  scaling : ∀ A : Set (Rd d), MeasurableSet A → ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c →
    78	    Γ (c • A) = ENNReal.ofReal (c ^ ((d : ℝ) - alpha)) * Γ A
    79	  threshold : alpha0 + alpha < 2
    80	  alpha_range : (0 < alpha ∧ alpha < d) ∨ (alpha = d ∧ d = 1)

    82	/-- The numerical part of `H:homog`, in the form used by `DriverParameters`

    84	theorem homog_params {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}

    86	    DriverParameters.Homog d alpha alpha0 :=

    93	    KappaRange.kappa alpha alpha0 ∈ Set.Ioo 1 2 :=
    94	  KappaRange.kappa_mem_Ioo d alpha alpha0 h.dim h.alpha0_pos h.alpha0_lt_one

    12	\begin{lemma}[The physical two-point integral]\label{L:spatial-physical-pair}
    13	  The positive measure $\nu(\ud x,\ud y) = \ud x\,\Gamma(\ud y)$ is
    14	  sigma-finite. For nonnegative functions define
    15	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-physical-pair}
    16	    B_\Gamma(f,h)=\int f(x)h(x-y)\nu(\ud x,\ud y)
    17	  \end{equation}
    18	  initially as an extended nonnegative integral, using finite Borel
    19	  representatives of Lebesgue classes. Its value is representative independent.
    20	  Lebesgue-a.e. convergence transfers to $\nu$-a.e. convergence at both
    21	  positions $x$ and $x-y$.
    22	\end{lemma}
    23	
    24	\begin{proof}
    25	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ gives sigma-finiteness on exhausting balls, and
    26	  Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite. If $N$ is Borel and Lebesgue null, Tonelli
    27	  applied first in $x$ gives $\nu\{x\in N\} = 0$ and $\nu\{x-y\in N\} = 0$,
    28	  because every fixed translate of $N$ is null. An arbitrary Lebesgue null set
    29	  has a Borel null superset. Thus, arbitrary versions are measurable in the
    30	  $\nu$ completion with the same value, and the same observation applies to the
    31	  exceptional sets of a.e. convergence. Signed pairings will be used only after
    32	  absolute convergence. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}.
    33	\end{proof}

    35	Put $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g) = B_\Gamma(g^2,g^2)$ and $b(g) = \|\nabla g\|_2^2$ on
    36	$H^1$; initially $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ is used only for smooth compact profiles
    37	before the extension below. For smooth compact $z$, write $U_z = \Gamma*z$ in
    38	its usual pointwise sense.

    40	\begin{lemma}[Smooth temporal controls]\label{L:spatial-static-controls}
    41	  For every nonnegative nonzero $z \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$, let
    42	  \[

    44	    \sup_{\substack{g\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|g\|_2=1}}
    45	    \left(c\int U_zg^2-b(g)\right),\qquad c>0.
    46	  \]
    47	  This is positive and finite, and $\lambda_z$ is Lipschitz on every compact
    48	  positive $c$ interval. With the exact $M_a$
    49	  in~\eqref{E:temporal-equilibrium-mass},
    50	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-static-score}
    51	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge
    52	    \lambda_z(1)-\frac{M_a}{2}B_\Gamma(z,z).

    55	
    56	\begin{proof}
    57	  Choose nonnegative nonzero $f \in C_c^\infty(0,1)$ and $s_0 = 1/2$. Let
    58	  $k_f(s_0) = \int_0^1|s_0-t|^{-a}f(t)\ud t > 0$. The smooth test $\Psi(t,x) =
    59	  cf(t)z(x)/k_f(s_0)$ has mean $cU_z$ at $s_0$.
    60	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate} gives boundedness of this
    61	  potential, the displayed real Rayleigh formula, and a positive rate for every
    62	  $c > 0$. Comparing identical unit tests makes $\lambda_z(c)^2$ Lipschitz with
    63	  constant $\|U_z\|_\infty$. On a positive compact interval its rate has a
    64	  positive floor by monotonicity, giving the square-root Lipschitz bound.
    65	
    66	  Use the nonincreasing smooth cutoff $\chi$ constructed in the proof of
    67	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-remove-mask}. For integers $n \ge 4$, set on
    68	  $(0,1)$
    69	  \[
    70	    f_n(t)=f_a(t)\chi(1/(nt))\chi(1/(n(1-t))),\qquad
    71	    k_n(s)=\int_0^1|s-t|^{-a}f_n(t)\ud t.
    72	  \]
    73	  Extend $f_n$ by zero. It is smooth compact, vanishes near both endpoints, is
    74	  nonzero, and increases to $f_a$. Thus, $\Psi_n = f_n\otimes z$ is a positive
    75	  smooth control. Monotone convergence
    76	  and~\eqref{E:temporal-equilibrium-potential} give $k_n(s)\uparrow1$ for every
    77	  $s \in [0,1]$. Since the kernel is at least one on the unit square off its
    78	  null diagonal, $0 < c_0: = \int_0^1f_4 \le k_n(s) \le 1$. The mean is
    79	  $k_n(s)U_z$; hence its rate is $\lambda_z(k_n(s))$, converging to
    80	  $\lambda_z(1)$ and bounded by that finite number. Dominated convergence gives
    81	  $I_{\Psi_n} \to \lambda_z(1)$.
    82	
    83	  The Gaussian cost is exactly the nonnegative Tonelli pairing
    84	  \[
    85	    v_{\Psi_n}=B_\Gamma(z,z)\int_0^1f_n(s)k_n(s)\ud s.

    88	  $M_aB_\Gamma(z,z)$. The spatial factor is finite and positive: its smooth
    89	  compact autocorrelation is positive near zero, and homogeneity scales any
    90	  origin-centered ball of positive $\Gamma$ mass to every other positive radius.

    92	  inequalities $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}} \ge I_{\Psi_n}-v_{\Psi_n}/2$. The variational
    93	  expression differences need not increase. No control depends on original large
    94	  time and no rough stochastic evolution has been used. This proves

    96	\end{proof}

    98	\begin{proposition}[The finite smooth spatial ratio]
    99	  \label{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}
   100	  For real unit $g \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$ put $R(g) =
   101	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)/b(g)^{\alpha/2}$. Its supremum $R_0$ over these profiles is
   102	  a positive finite real number, and
   103	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-smooth-score}
   104	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge
   105	    k\left[
   106	    \frac{R(g)\alpha^{\alpha/2}}{8M_aq^{q/2}}
   107	    \right]^{1/k}.
   108	  \end{equation}
   109	\end{proposition}
   110	
   111	\begin{proof}
   112	  The gradient energy $b(g)$ is positive: a nonzero $L^2$ function with zero
   113	  weak gradient would have Fourier transform supported only at zero, and hence
   114	  would vanish. Its square is nonnegative nonzero smooth compact, so the
   115	  autocorrelation argument in the preceding proof gives $0 < A: =
   116	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g) < \infty$. With $U_\ell g(x) = \ell^{d/2}g(\ell x)$, the
   117	  physical changes of variables give
   118	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-dilation}
   119	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(U_\ell g)=\ell^\alpha A,\qquad
   120	    b(U_\ell g)=\ell^2b(g).
   121	  \end{equation}
   122	  The factors in the first identity are $\ell^{2d}$ from the two squares,
   123	  $\ell^{-d}$ from $\ud x$, and $\ell^{\alpha-d}$ from the Radon pushforward.
   124	
   125	  For $\theta,\ell > 0$ choose the smooth control $z = \theta(U_\ell g)^2$. The
   126	  Rayleigh test $U_\ell g$ gives $\lambda_z(1)^2 \ge \theta\ell^\alpha
   127	  A-\ell^2b$, while $B_\Gamma(z,z) = \theta^2\ell^\alpha A$. For any $L > 0$,
   128	  put $u = \alpha/q > 0$ and choose
   129	  \[
   130	    \ell^2=uL^2/b,\qquad
   131	    \theta=(1+u)L^2/(\ell^\alpha A).
   132	  \]
   133	  The radicand is $L^2$. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls} consequently
   134	  gives
   135	  \[
   136	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge L-CL^q,\qquad
   137	    C=\frac{M_a(1+u)^2}{2R(g)u^{\alpha/2}}>0.
   138	  \]
   139	  Its maximum occurs at $L^k = 1/(qC)$ and is $(k/q)(qC)^{-1/k}$. Since $1+u =
   140	  4/q$, $1/(q^qC) = R(g)\alpha^{\alpha/2}/(8M_aq^{q/2})$,
   141	  proving~\eqref{E:spatial-smooth-score}. The already finite
   142	  $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$ bounds every ratio by
   143	  $8M_aq^{q/2}(S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}/k)^k/\alpha^{\alpha/2}$. A normalized compact
   144	  bump supplies a positive ratio. This proves positivity and finiteness of $R_0$
   145	  before any rough spatial extension is invoked. This proves
   146	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}.
   147	\end{proof}

   173	  absolute correlation is compactly supported and bounded by $\|Q\|_2\|P\|_2$.

   175	  Smooth signed covariance is positive: with the ordinary transform
   176	  $\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot x}Q(x)\ud x$, the model
   177	  convention gives
   178	  \[
   179	    B_\Gamma(Q,Q)=\int|\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi)
   180	    \ge0,\qquad Q\in C_c^\infty(\R^d;\R).
   181	  \]
   182	  Pair $\Gamma$ with the smooth compact correlation to obtain this identity;
   183	  rapid Fourier decay and tempered $\mu$ give finiteness. Evenness of $\Gamma$
   184	  and $(x,y)\mapsto(x-y,-y)$ give symmetry. The quadratic polynomial for $Q+tP$

   187	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   188	    \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2.

   193	  radius-$R$ ball, vanishing beyond $2R$ and with gradient at most $C/R$,
   194	  converge by the function and gradient tails and the bound $C\|f\|_2/R$ for the
   195	  extra gradient term. Mollification then converges in $H^1$ by $L^2$
   196	  translation continuity of the function and its weak gradients. The space is
   197	  separable through its closed isometric image $f\mapsto(f,\nabla f)$ in

   282	Define, for $u \ne 0$,

   284	  K_\star(u)=\frac1{\Gamma_E(a)}

   291	\begin{lemma}[Exact row maximum]\label{L:occupation-kernel-row}
   292	  The kernel is even, positive off zero, locally integrable, decreasing on
   293	  $(0,\infty)$, and $K_\star(u) \le |u|^{-a}$ off zero. Its exact row maximum on
   294	  $[0,1]$ is
   295	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-kernel-row}
   296	    \max_{s\in[0,1]}\int_0^1K_\star(s-t)\ud t

   298	  \end{equation}
   299	\end{lemma}

   301	\begin{proof}
   302	  Dropping the positive quadratic damping bounds the mixture by the Gamma
   303	  integral $|u|^{-a}$. Positivity and monotonicity follow directly from the
   304	  integrand, and $a < 1$ gives local integrability. Put $\Phi(t) =
   305	  \int_0^tK_\star(u)\ud u$. It is concave because its integrand is decreasing on
   306	  positive arguments. The row is $\Phi(s)+\Phi(1-s) \le 2\Phi(1/2)$, with
   307	  equality at $s = 1/2$. The diagonal value changes no time integral. This
   308	  proves Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-kernel-row}.
   309	\end{proof}

   386	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. For `F` integrable on `X × (Y × Z)`, the iterated
   387	integrals in the orders
   388	`z, y, x` and `x, y, z` agree. -/
   389	theorem iterated_integral_swap {X Y Z : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] [MeasurableSpace Y]
   390	    [MeasurableSpace Z] {μX : Measure X} {μY : Measure Y} {μZ : Measure Z} [SFinite μX]
   391	    [SFinite μY] [SFinite μZ] (F : X × (Y × Z) → ℝ)
   392	    (hF : Integrable F (μX.prod (μY.prod μZ))) :
   393	    ∫ z, ∫ y, ∫ x, F (x, (y, z)) ∂μX ∂μY ∂μZ =
   394	      ∫ x, ∫ y, ∫ z, F (x, (y, z)) ∂μZ ∂μY ∂μX := by
   395	  have h1 := integral_prod F hF
   396	  have h2 := integral_prod_symm F hF
   397	  have hG : Integrable (fun yz : Y × Z => ∫ x, F (x, yz) ∂μX) (μY.prod μZ) :=
   398	    hF.integral_prod_right
   399	  have h3 := integral_prod_symm _ hG
   400	  have h4 : (fun x => ∫ yz, F (x, yz) ∂(μY.prod μZ)) =ᵐ[μX]
   401	      fun x => ∫ y, ∫ z, F (x, (y, z)) ∂μZ ∂μY :=
   402	    hF.prod_right_ae.mono fun x hx => integral_prod _ hx
   403	  rw [← h3, ← h2, h1]
   404	  exact integral_congr_ae h4

   407	two-time kernel, with
   408	the time variables innermost. -/
   409	theorem lintegral_triple_twoTime {X Y : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] [MeasurableSpace Y]
   410	    (ν : Measure X) (μ : Measure Y) [SFinite ν] [SFinite μ] (f c A : X → Y → ℝ)
   411	    (hf : Measurable (Function.uncurry f)) (hc : Measurable (Function.uncurry c))
   412	    (hA : Measurable (Function.uncurry A)) (hf0 : ∀ x y, 0 ≤ f x y)
   413	    (hc0 : ∀ x y, 0 < c x y) (hA0 : ∀ x y, 0 ≤ A x y) :
   414	    ∫⁻ z, ENNReal.ofReal (f z.1 z.2.1 * twoTimeR (c z.1 z.2.1) (A z.1 z.2.1) z.2.2)
   415	        ∂(ν.prod (μ.prod P2)) =
   416	      ∫⁻ x, ∫⁻ y, ENNReal.ofReal (f x y / (c x y * (c x y + A x y))) ∂μ ∂ν := by
   417	  have hmeas : Measurable fun z : X × (Y × (ℝ × ℝ)) =>
   418	      ENNReal.ofReal (f z.1 z.2.1 * twoTimeR (c z.1 z.2.1) (A z.1 z.2.1) z.2.2) := by
   419	    have e1 : Measurable fun z : X × (Y × (ℝ × ℝ)) => f z.1 z.2.1 :=
   420	      hf.comp (measurable_fst.prodMk measurable_snd.fst)
   421	    have e2 : Measurable fun z : X × (Y × (ℝ × ℝ)) => c z.1 z.2.1 :=
   422	      hc.comp (measurable_fst.prodMk measurable_snd.fst)
   423	    have e3 : Measurable fun z : X × (Y × (ℝ × ℝ)) => A z.1 z.2.1 :=
   424	      hA.comp (measurable_fst.prodMk measurable_snd.fst)
   425	    unfold twoTimeR
   426	    fun_prop
   427	  rw [lintegral_prod _ hmeas.aemeasurable]
   428	  refine lintegral_congr fun x => ?_
   429	  have hm2 : Measurable fun yp : Y × (ℝ × ℝ) =>
   430	      ENNReal.ofReal (f x yp.1 * twoTimeR (c x yp.1) (A x yp.1) yp.2) :=
   431	    hmeas.comp measurable_prodMk_left
   432	  dsimp only
   433	  rw [lintegral_prod _ hm2.aemeasurable]
   434	  refine lintegral_congr fun y => ?_
   435	  simp_rw [ENNReal.ofReal_mul (hf0 x y)]
   436	  rw [lintegral_const_mul _ ?_, twoTimeR_lintegral _ _ (hc0 x y) (hA0 x y),
   437	    ← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (hf0 x y)]

  1755	
  1756	Formalizes two lemmas of the section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`
  1757	(`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` at `3920258`; the file is
  1758	byte-identical at `ba01d98`, so the line numbers agree):
  1759	`L:occupation-kernel-row` (lines 291-309) with the kernel
  1760	`E:occupation-damped-kernel` (lines 282-289) and the display
  1761	`E:occupation-kernel-row` (lines 295-298), and `L:spatial-physical-pair`
  1762	(lines 12-33) with `E:spatial-physical-pair` (lines 15-17). Nothing is
  1763	supplied as a hypothesis. `Kstar` is the manuscript's formula word for word,
  1764	with `K_star(0) = 0` (line 289) and `Gamma_E` read as Mathlib's
  1765	`Real.Gamma`. `Kstar_eq_Psi` identifies it, for `u != 0`, with the averaged
  1766	clock kernel `TimeFractional.Psi a |u| (|u|/D)` (main file,
  1767	`E:averaged-clock-kernel`, line 7503), and positivity and the bound
  1768	`K_star(u) <= |u|^(-a)` are reused from `TimeFractional`.
  1769	`kstarIntegrand_integrable` proves that the defining integral converges for
  1770	`a > 0`, `D > 0`, `u != 0`. It is a separate theorem, not a conjunct of the
  1771	headline. The headline `occupation_kernel_row` (for `0 < a < 1`, `D > 0`)
  1772	proves exactly nine conjuncts: evenness; positivity off zero; local
  1773	integrability; strict decrease on `(0,inf)` (the TeX says "decreasing", which
  1774	this implies); `K_star(u) <= |u|^(-a)` off zero; interval integrability of
  1775	each row `t -> K_star(s-t)`, `s` in `[0,1]`, on `[0,1]`; that
  1776	`R_star = 2 int_0^(1/2) K_star` is the greatest element of the set of row
  1777	values over `s` in `[0,1]` (so the maximum exists, equals `R_star` and is
  1778	attained at `s = 1/2`); interval integrability of `K_star` on `[0,1/2]`; and
  1779	`0 < R_star` (a real number, hence finite). `occupation_kernel_row_paper`
  1780	states this under the section's standing assumptions (lines 4-10: `H:homog`
  1781	as `HomogCovariance d alpha a Gamma mu` with `a = alpha0`, `Gamma != 0`,
  1782	`D = (4 - alpha) - 2a`). `D > 0` and `a < 1` are derived from `H:homog`
  1783	(`a + alpha < 2`, `a < 1`); `Gamma != 0` and the other clauses of `H:homog`
  1784	are carried and not used. The TeX proof shows the row bound
  1785	`Phi(s) + Phi(1-s) <= 2 Phi(1/2)` by concavity of `Phi`. Lean proves it
  1786	instead by a shift comparison that uses the same monotonicity of `K_star`
  1787	(`Phi_sum_le_of_le_half`, auxiliary). For `L:spatial-physical-pair`,
  1788	`pairMeasure Gamma = volume.prod Gamma` on `R^d x R^d` (`EuclideanSpace`),
  1789	and `pairing` is the lower Lebesgue integral of `f(x) h(x-y)` for
  1790	`[0,inf]`-valued `f, h`. This allows arbitrary `[0,inf]`-valued functions,
  1791	a class that contains the TeX's finite Borel representatives.

   150	\chapter{Setting and strategy}\label{S:book-setting}
   151	
   152	\section{Model and standing assumptions}\label{S:model}
   153	
   154	We study the hyperbolic Anderson model
   155	\cite{chen:author2026:time-dependency}*{(1.1)}
   156	\begin{equation}\label{E:HAM}
   157	  \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}(t,x)=\Delta u(t,x)+\W(t,x)u(t,x),
   158	  \qquad u(0,x)=1,\quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}(0,x)=0,
   159	\end{equation}
   160	for $(t,x) \in \R_+\times\R^d$, $d \in \{1,2,3\}$, interpreted in the
   161	Stratonovich sense (limit of classical wave equations driven by smoothed noises
   162	$\W_{\epsilon,\delta}$). The noise is centered Gaussian with
   163	\begin{equation}\label{E:cov}
   164	  \operatorname{Cov}\big(\W(s,x),\W(t,y)\big)=|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}\gamma(x-y),
   165	  \qquad 0<\alpha_0<1,
   166	\end{equation}
   167	where $\gamma \ge 0$ is nonnegative definite with spectral measure $\mu$.
   168	
   169	\begin{hypothesis}[Homogeneous covariance]\label{H:homog}
   170	  Let $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha_0 < 1$. The spatial covariance is a
   171	  nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$ on
   172	  $\R^d$, with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure $\mu$ in the
   173	  convention
   174	  \[
   175	    \Gamma=\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}\mu(\ud\xi)
   176	    \quad\text{in the sense of tempered distributions}.
   177	  \]
   178	  The symbol $\gamma$ in~\eqref{E:cov} denotes this covariance as a function
   179	  when one exists, and as a distribution otherwise. For every Borel set $A$ and
   180	  $c > 0$, $\Gamma(cA) = c^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$, and
   181	  \begin{equation}\label{E:threshold}
   182	    \alpha_0+\alpha<2,
   183	  \end{equation}
   184	  with $0 < \alpha < d$, or $\alpha = d = 1$. In particular, the last case
   185	  includes spatial white noise $\Gamma = \delta_0$.
   186	\end{hypothesis}
   187	
   188	Throughout we write
   189	\begin{equation}\label{E:kappa}
   190	  \kappa:=\frac{4-\alpha-\alpha_0}{3-\alpha}\in(1,2).
   191	\end{equation}
   192	
   193	\paragraph{Contribution of the present work.}
   194	We address the second moment of the original Stratonovich solution with
   195	fractional temporal covariance throughout Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}. The
   196	independent upper bound reaches the scale $t^\kappa$, rather than only the
   197	coarse quadratic exponential scale in the source. The main identification gives
   198	an intrinsic variational expression for the limiting constant over all
   199	nonnegative smooth compact spacetime controls, without a separability
   200	restriction. It retains the covariance amplitude, kinetic coefficient one and a
   201	Gaussian cost equal to one half of the variance, and includes the zero
   202	covariance case. The upper and lower comparisons refer to the same canonical
   203	solution. The occupation and spatial-energy estimates then give bounds on this
   204	constant; evaluating the white spatial energy is not a numerical evaluation of
   205	the full moment supremum. The earlier results discussed below concern different
   206	stochastic interpretations or temporal covariances and do not supply this
   207	identification by substitution.
   208	
   209	Figure~\ref{Fig:proof-map} summarizes the main dependencies.
   210	\input{notes/figures/proof-map}
   211	
   212	\paragraph{Main result and dependencies.}
   213	Theorem~\ref{T:intrinsic-second-moment} identifies the original point-moment
   214	limit for every covariance in Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}. Its full variational
   215	domain and normalization are displayed in~\eqref{E:intrinsic-positive-formula}.
   216	Theorem~\ref{T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling} and
   217	Corollary~\ref{C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket} give derived bounds;
   218	Section~\ref{S:intrinsic-white-evaluation} evaluates the white spatial energy
   219	and its resulting moment bounds. These bounds need not be attained at the moment
   220	constant.

  1207	
  1208	States Hypothesis `H:homog` (main TeX file, Section `S:model`) in full as
  1209	the predicate `HomogCovariance`, and restates `E:kappa` and
  1210	`E:driver-parameters` under it. The manuscript's Fourier convention
  1211	`Gamma = int e^(i xi.x) mu(d xi)` is written out explicitly rather than
  1212	through Mathlib's Fourier transform. A Lean measure is nonnegative, and on
  1213	`R^d` a locally finite Borel measure is a Radon measure. The proofs of the
  1214	two restated results use only the numerical part of the hypothesis.
